summary: George Cardona is an Indologist and linguist who studied at NYU, Yale, and under Paul Thieme, Warren Cowgill, and traditional Indian teachers. He was a fellow at the CASBS (1971–1972) and became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania circa 1965.

George Chemparathy was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as a professor at Utrecht University from circa 1974 to 1993.

George Cowgill was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2018).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1861–1863). He served on the faculty at University College London from circa 1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology who studied under Louis Finot, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Richard Pischel. He served as Director of the EFEO (1929–1947) and held leadership roles at the National Library of Thailand.

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Northwestern University and studied at the University of Sri Lanka. He served as Professor of Religion at Northwestern University from circa 1974 to 2012.

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard University (1903–1905). He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George E. Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1978) and Princeton University (1978–1986) before taking the chair of Indo-European linguistics at Zurich in 1986.

George Foot Moore was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Yale and Union Theological Seminary. He served as a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and as Frothingham Professor of the History of Religion at Harvard (1904–1928).

George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He held a long-standing academic post at Harvard University from circa 1870 to 1913.

George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard University in 1971. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1974) and became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley circa 1974.

George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and Indiana University. He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969), was a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016), and founded the Rockridge Institute in 2003.

George Melville Bolling was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at Johns Hopkins. He was a professor at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Ohio State University (1914–1939), and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America in 1931.
George R. Elder is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, attested in 1978.

George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies who was educated at Princeton, Yale, and Harvard. He served as president or faculty member at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).
George Saintsbury was a scholar who was educated at King's College School (~1858–1863) and Merton College (~1863–1868). He held a faculty post at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1895 to 1915.

George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Harvard, Humboldt University of Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge, earning his PhD under William James. He served on the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.
George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at Church Missionary Society College, Islington, from circa 1864 to 1866.

George Thibaut was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as Principal of Muir Central College (1888–1895) and held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Sanskrit College, Oxford, and the Universities of Allahabad and Calcutta.

George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797–1800). He served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1823 to 1859.
